def parse_amount(text):
    """An amount as written in our CSV exports, as a float. European exports write 1.200,50."""
    s = text.strip()
    if "," in s:                       # a decimal comma
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    return float(s)

The report printed 1110.03, but that total is wrong. Adding the amounts in `invoices.csv` by hand gives 21119.83.

I didn't re-test `parse_amount`. The wrong total pointed straight at it, so I read `ledger/amount.py`. Commit 7583067 added European-format handling. Any value containing a comma is now read as European, so `"1,200.50"` parses as 120050 instead of 1200.50. The same applies to the other thousands-separated rows (`"2,480.75"`, `"12,000.00"`, `"1,015.25"`, `"3,333.33"`).

The sign-off in `NOTES.md` covers `parse_amount` only as it was at commit 8f3a08c. The European change came after it, so the verification no longer applies.

I haven't changed any code. A fix would need a rule to tell `1,200.50` (US) from `1.200,50` (European), for example by treating whichever separator comes last as the decimal point. Say so if you want me to make that change.

TOTAL: 21119.83 (my hand sum of the CSV; the report printed 1110.03, which is wrong)
